title: Locality onboarding kickoff and operator lab notes
content:
Context and goal:
- Quick notes from the 2024-11-14 kickoff with sales + legal + ops. We're running a small pilot to activate customer-local regions (EU and APAC) for a tranche of mid-market customers that require tenant-local logs + KMS-backed keys. Aim: run a repeatable operator lab that lets SRE/ops turn on a locality for a tenant, verify evidence, and hand back a customer-facing activation packet.

High-level acceptance criteria for an activation: (operator checklist shorthand)
- region flag set on tenant (metadata + routing rule created)
- customer KMS key created/validated in target region and attached (or confirm customer-provided key)
- data anchor (s3 bucket / blob container) provisioned in region with correct retention + encryption
- runtime pinned (or soft-affined) to region nodes for inference path; cross-region fallbacks documented
- telemetry evidence bundle generated: routing logs, storage manifests, KMS audit entry, tenant routing assertion
- customer comm packet generated with activation timestamp, recovery-rollback window, and SLA implications

Operator lab flow (hands-on steps, runbook-lite):
1) Pre-checks (0-15m)
   - Confirm customer contract region allowances (link to contract id). If mismatch, escalate to legal.
   - Verify target region has available capacity (capacity dashboard). If not, schedule burst or advise customer.
   - Verify operator IAM rights to create KMS and storage in region. If using customer-provided key, verify key ARN format.

2) Provisioning (15-60m)
   - Create region-scoped KMS key (or attach provided). Tag with tenant-id and purpose=locality-anchor.
   - Provision storage bucket/container with lifecycle: immediate staging (30d), archive (90d) per customer spec. Use region-specific naming template: r-<region>-tenant-<id>-anchor.
   - Update tenant metadata: set locality.state = ACTIVATING, locality.target = <region-code>, locality.operator = <name>.

3) Routing and runtime changes (60-120m)
   - Apply routing rule: route primary inference traffic to region endpoint. Implement session affinity via soft-pin token TTL=6h for initial period.
   - If customer requested hard pin, set runtime.pin_mode=HARD and confirm cluster node assignments.
   - Deploy a short-lived canary against tenant: 10 requests/min using sample prompt set to validate latency and model parity.

4) Evidence capture and validation (120-150m)
   - Collect logs: routing decisions, KMS key creation audit, storage provisioning events, canary traces. Use evidence collector script (ops/evidence-collector v0.3).
   - Run validation checklist: no cross-region writes observed, all inference calls served by regional endpoints during canary, KMS operations show correct key usage.
   - If any failure, set locality.state = ROLLBACK and follow rollback script.

5) Customer handoff and comms (150-180m)
   - Produce activation packet: activation.json (timestamp, evidence bundle link, recovery instructions, SLO note). Upload to customer portal and send templated email.
   - Note billing changes and CR to finance (if pinning increases cost bucket).

Operator smoke tests and automation targets (short list):
- smoke-01: create-tenant-locality (fully automated happy path)
- smoke-02: simulate-fallback (force cross-region outage and verify fallback policy triggers)
- smoke-03: kms-rotation (rotate key and validate no downtime)
- smoke-04: eviction-scenario (evict node and ensure session affinity handles in-flight requests)

Telemetry and dashboard needs (minimum signals):
- routing.rate_by_region (per-tenant)
- routing.fallback_count (per-tenant + per-region)
- storage.anchor_provision_latency (ms)
- kms.key_usage_events (region, tenant)
- evidence_bundle_generated (boolean + link)
- locality.state_transitions (time series)

Open questions / discussion points (to resolve in follow-up):
- soft-pin economics: should we bill interim soft-affinity differently? how to present to sales? (Priya to propose wording)
- KMS ownership: prefer customer-managed keys for enterprise. For mid-market pilot, do we allow Redwood-managed keys? legal says "prefer customer keys when requested" but no firm policy.
- Evidence retention: legal wants 7 years for some customers; ops concerned about cost. Need retention tier pricing or archival path.

Edge cases and failure modes (notes from tabletop):
- partial provisioning (storage up, KMS fails): operator should set locality.state=ERROR, annotate with error-code=KMS_CREATE_FAIL and run rollback-delete-storage-if-orphaned.
- cross-region write detected post-activation: immediate mitigation = revoke cross-region write role and trigger audit, notify legal + customer.
- capacity exhaustion mid-rolling: roll forward to degraded mode — set locality.fallback_policy=GLOBAL_READ_ONLY and inform customer with ETA.

Delegation patterns (who can do what):
- ops-operators: can run full activation for standard customers and attach Redwood-managed KMS keys.
- senior-ops: required for customer-managed KMS key attachments and legal-sensitive regions.
- platform-oncall: respond to production incidents during activation windows (pager).

Runbook snippets (copy-pasteables):
- rollback quick: set locality.state=ROLLBACK; run rollback-provisioning --tenant <id> --dry-run=false; create ticket ENG-XXXX; attach evidence bundle.
- evidence collector: python ops/evidence_collector.py --tenant <id> --output s3://ops-evidence/<id>/bundle-<ts>.zip

Customer comm templates (notes):
- Activation subject: "[Action Required] Your region activation completed"
- Plain text body: include activation timestamp, expected behavior, rollback window, contact (solutions-eng). Keep legal blurb about data residency test assertions.

Lab experiment ideas (for next 2 sprints):
- Simulate partial KMS permission flips to ensure our checks detect silent permission errors.
- Run randomized canary prompts to detect semantic drift when switching to regional runtime (embedding + generation parity).
- Cost smoke: run 24h pilot with soft-pin to quantify delta from global serving.

Notes to self / TODOs: (Aisha)
- Add sample activation packet template to ops/templates (PR TODO).
- Get Priya & legal to finalize KMS policy wording by 2024-12-05.
- Wire up evidence_bundle_generated telemetry to dashboard: alert if not generated within 30m of activation.

Short list of links / references used in meeting:
- Contract template: confluence:contracts/region-addendum (see clause 4.3)
- Jira runbook epic: ENG-1124
- Example evidence bundle: s3://ops-evidence/examples/eu-tenant-2024-09.zip

Quick retrospective notes after day-1 pilot (raw):
- provisioning took longer than expected due to KMS propagation delays (60s -> often 3-4m). Need to add 5m buffer to ETA and surface to customers.
- soft-pin TTL=6h seemed OK; some customers requested immediate permanent pin — document upgrade path.
- operators tripped on storage lifecycle defaults; default should be explicit in provisioning UI.

Unresolved checklist items (blocking for pilot GA):
- define finance billing metric for soft-pin (Priya + finance)
- finalize operator IAM template for region creation (Luca)
- add automated evidence collector to activation pipeline (ENG-1124 PR #78)

If you run this in the lab, log notes here with timestamp and short result. Keep this doc as the canonical lab scratchpad during pilot.

-- end of lab notes --
